definitions.explanation: Writing done quickly and carelessly, resulting in messy, hard-to-read text. The image is of striking the paper rather than carefully forming characters.

examples.japanese: ⟦メモ→メモ：00274_memo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{殴|なぐ}り{書|が}き⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。

examples.english: His handwriting is such a scrawl that I can't read it.

examples.japanese: ⟦{急|いそ}いでいた→急ぐ：01191_isogu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、{殴|なぐ}り{書|が}き⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦メモ→メモ：00274_memo⟧⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧⟦{残|のこ}して→残す：01975_nokosu⟧⟦{出|で}かけた→出かける：00833_dekakeru⟧。
examples.english: Since I was in a hurry, I left just a hastily scrawled note and went out.

notes:
Writing done quickly and carelessly, resulting in messy, hard-to-read text.

ETYMOLOGY:
⟦{殴|なぐ}る→殴る：02378_naguru⟧ (to hit/punch) + ⟦{書|か}き→書く：00477_kaku⟧ (writing). The vivid image is of striking the paper with a pen rather than carefully forming characters.

COMMON PATTERNS:
Functions as both a noun and a ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ verb:
- {殴|なぐ}り{書|が}き⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦メモ→メモ：00274_memo⟧: a scrawled memo (noun)
- ⟦メモ→メモ：00274_memo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{殴|なぐ}り{書|が}き⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to scribble a memo (verb)

USAGE:
Often slightly self-deprecating or humorous. Used when jotting something down in a hurry without caring about neatness. Not typically used to criticize someone else's handwriting directly — for that, ⟦{字|じ}→字：01606_ji⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{汚|きたな}い→汚い：00788_kitanai⟧ (messy handwriting) is more common.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{走|はし}り{書|が}き→走り書き：25864_hashirigaki⟧: hasty writing (similar meaning, less vivid)
- ⟦{落書|らくが}き→落書き：14043_rakugaki⟧: doodling, graffiti (different — drawing rather than writing)
